dhpak1.12:1.1: 1.11 The Story about the Lay Disciple Dhammika Dhammika-Upāsakassa Vatthu
dhpak1.12:2.1: “Here he rejoices, after death he rejoices,” {1.129} this Dhamma teaching was given by the Teacher while he was in residence
dhpak1.12:2.2: at Jetavana with reference to the lay disciple Dhammika.
dhpak1.12:3.1: At Sāvatthī, we are told, lived five hundred lay people called Dhammika,
dhpak1.12:3.2: each with a retinue of five hundred lay friends.
dhpak1.12:3.3: The senior lay disciple had seven sons and seven daughters.
dhpak1.12:3.4: Each of these sons regularly gave ticket-porridge, ticket-food, food of the waning moon, food of the new moon, invitation-food,
dhpak1.12:3.5: the Observance Day food, visitors’ food, and food during the season of the rains.
dhpak1.12:3.6: All of them took after their father, so that the lay disciple and his wife and fourteen children maintained sixteen forms of alms.
dhpak1.12:3.7: And the lay disciple, virtuous, upright, together with son and wife, took delight in the distribution of alms.
dhpak1.12:4.1: Life of Generosity After a time the lay disciple was attacked by a disease, and his vital forces began to decay. {1.130}
dhpak1.12:4.2: Desiring to hear the Dhamma, he sent word to the Teacher: “Send me eight or sixteen bhikkhus.”
dhpak1.12:4.3: The Teacher sent them, and they straightaway went and gathered around his bed and sat down on seats prepared for them.
dhpak1.12:4.4: “Venerable Sirs,” said the lay disciple, “it will be difficult for me to see you, for I am weak; tell me but a single Discourse.”
dhpak1.12:4.5: – “Which Discourse would you like to hear, lay brother?”
dhpak1.12:4.6: – “The Mindfulness Discourse, common to all the Buddhas.”
dhpak1.12:4.7: Accordingly they began to rehearse the Discourse, beginning with the words: “This is a one-way path, bhikkhus, for the purification of beings.”
dhpak1.12:5.1: At that moment, from the six worlds of the Devas, approached six chariots a 150 leagues long, drawn by a thousand Sindh horses,
dhpak1.12:5.3: In each chariot stood a Devatā, and each Devatā spoke and said: “Permit us to convey you to our celestial world.”
dhpak1.12:5.4: And they spoke again and said: “Even as one shatters a clay vessel and replaces it with a vessel of gold,
dhpak1.12:5.5: even so are [28.229] living beings reborn to take their pleasure in our celestial world.”
dhpak1.12:5.6: The lay disciple, unwilling to be interrupted in listening to the Dhamma, said: “Wait! Wait!”
dhpak1.12:5.7: The bhikkhus, thinking that he was speaking to them, ceased their recitation of the Dhamma.
dhpak1.12:5.8: His sons and daughters cried out: “Formerly our father could never hear enough of the Dhamma. But now, after summoning
dhpak1.12:5.9: the bhikkhus and directing them to rehearse the Dhamma, he stops them himself. After all, there is no man who does not fear death.”
dhpak1.12:5.10: The bhikkhus said to each other: “This is no time for us to remain.” And forthwith they arose and departed.
dhpak1.12:6.1: After a time the lay disciple recovered his attention and asked his sons: “Why do you weep?”
dhpak1.12:6.2: – “Dear father,” said they, “you sent for the bhikkhus, and even as you listened to the Dhamma, you yourself stopped them
dhpak1.12:6.3: from rehearsing the Dhamma. We weep to think: ‘After all, there is no man who does not fear death.’”
dhpak1.12:6.6: – “They said to each other: ‘This is no time for us to remain.’ And forthwith they arose from their seats and departed.”
dhpak1.12:6.7: – “Dear sons, I was not speaking to the noble ones.”
dhpak1.12:6.8: – “With whom, then, were you talking, dear father?”
dhpak1.12:6.9: – “From the six worlds of the Devas Devatās approached in six magnificently adorned chariots, and standing in their chariots
dhpak1.12:6.10: poised in the air, they said to me: ‘Take your pleasure in our celestial world; take your pleasure in our celestial world.’
dhpak1.12:6.12: – “Dear father, where are the chariots? We do not see them.”
dhpak1.12:6.15: – “Which celestial world is the most delightful?”
dhpak1.12:6.16: – “Dear father, the most delightful is the world of the Tusita gods, the abode of the mothers and fathers of the Buddhas and of all the Bodhisattas.”
dhpak1.12:6.17: – “Well then, throw a wreath of flowers and say: ‘Let this wreath of flowers cling to the chariot which came from the world of the Tusita gods.’”
dhpak1.12:7.1: Accordingly the children of the lay disciple threw the wreath of flowers, and it clung to the pole of the chariot and hung suspended in the air.
dhpak1.12:7.2: The populace saw the wreath of flowers suspended in the air, but did not see the chariot.
dhpak1.12:7.3: The lay disciple said: “Do you see this wreath of flowers?” – “Yes, we see it.”
dhpak1.12:7.4: – “This wreath hangs suspended from the chariot which came from the world of the Tusita gods. I am going to the world of the Tusita gods; be not disturbed.
dhpak1.12:7.5: If you desire to be reborn with me, do works of merit even as I have done.”
dhpak1.12:7.6: And when he had thus spoken, he died and set foot in the chariot.
dhpak1.12:7.7: Immediately he was reborn as a Deva three-quarters of a league in stature, adorned with sixty cartloads of ornaments.
dhpak1.12:7.8: A retinue of a thousand [28.230] Accharās attended him, and a golden mansion twenty-five leagues in extent became visible.
dhpak1.12:8.1: Celestial Worlds When those bhikkhus reached the monastery, the Teacher asked them: “Bhikkhus, did the lay disciple hearken
dhpak1.12:8.2: to the recitation of the Dhamma?”
dhpak1.12:8.3: – “Yes, venerable Sir. But in the midst of the recitation he cried out: ‘Wait! Wait!’ and stopped us.
dhpak1.12:8.4: Then his sons and daughters began to weep, {1.132}
dhpak1.12:8.5: whereupon we said to each other: ‘This is no time for us to remain,’ and arose from our seats and departed.”
dhpak1.12:8.6: – “Bhikkhus, he was not talking to you.
dhpak1.12:8.7: From the six worlds of the Devas Devatās approached in six magnificently adorned chariots, and they summoned that lay disciple to go with them;
dhpak1.12:8.8: but the lay disciple, unwilling that the recitation of the Dhamma should be interrupted, spoke to them.”
dhpak1.12:8.9: – “Is that true, venerable Sir?” – “That is true, bhikkhus.”
dhpak1.12:8.10: – “Venerable Sir, where was he reborn just now?”
dhpak1.12:8.11: – “In the world of the Tusita gods, bhikkhus.”
dhpak1.12:9.1: “Venerable Sir, but recently he lived here among his kinsfolk rejoicing, and just now he went again to a place of rejoicing and was there reborn.”
dhpak1.12:9.2: – “Yes, bhikkhus. They that are heedful, be they laymen or those gone forth, rejoice in both places equally.”
dhpak1.12:9.3: So saying, he pronounced the following verse:
dhpak1.12:10.1: 16. Idha modati, pecca modati, katapuñño ubhayattha modati, so modati, so pamodati, disvā kammavisuddhim-attano.
dhpak1.12:11.1: Here he rejoices, after death he rejoices, the righteous one rejoices in both places, he rejoices, he greatly rejoices, seeing the purity of his own deeds.
dhpak1.12:12.1: At the conclusion of the verse many became Stream-enterers and so on, and benefit arose to many people from the Dhamma teaching.
